code:
V.SHMUP LITE
Joystick 2: move / fire.

UPWARD FLIGHT: scenery moves down and repeats continuously. The shot starts at the ship nose.

WAVE_SCRIPT ($B000): 8 rows of 4 bytes: PATH, X, COUNT, GAP.
PATH: 0 straight, 1 left, 2 right, 3 zigzag, 4 sine.
X: entry/centre position. COUNT: enemies in the wave. GAP: frames between enemies.
Up to 4 enemies fly together. A 96-frame gap separates waves; the sequence repeats.
SINE_PATH ($B100) holds 128 signed offsets.

Every ordinary node contains ONE opcode. Open collapsed ORGs to edit. INIT and its startup nodes move together. Home finds INIT.

RAM: $2000 tiles, $2800 sprites, $3000 repeating map, $4000 splash, $8000 boot, $9000 setup, $A800 waves, $AC00 hits, $B000 tables, $C000 state.

FIXED HUD: existing IRQ HANDLER + two IRQ slots on the INIT spine. Installed after the splash. Line 32 fixes HUD scroll; line 69 switches to the playfield during the blank separator row. Payloads are individual opcodes in the $B200 ORG. Direct IRQ mode keeps KERNAL banked out; CIA interrupts are disabled and NMI has a safe RTI.

MENU MUSIC ONLY: Music Maker uses voices 1+2 on the title screen. Gameplay silences both voices.

GAME_SFX: open this SFX Maker asset to edit LASER (effect 0) and EXPLOSION (effect 1). Both use voice 3. Explosion priority 2 overrides laser priority 1.

EXPLOSIONS / SFX ($B300): SFX INIT prepares the bank on game entry; PLAY triggers fire or explosion; UPDATE runs once per game frame. No song switching or music restart. All four SFX nodes use GAME_SFX and voice 3.

Three burst frames show enemy/player destruction before removal/respawn. Ordinary nodes remain individual opcodes; no CODE blocks.

WORLD uses 4x4 metatiles: mirrored stone, cracked, vine and overgrown walls. Both walls are 32 pixels wide. Sprites 6/7 mask the wall entry row; enemies appear whole below the HUD at Y=80. Frame 9 is the wall mask; there are no sliced enemy-entry frames.
The playfield extends to the VIC bottom border (OMIT BOTTOM=0). Gameplay calculations run before the border wait. At raster 248, after the border closes, sprite registers are prepared and scrolling is updated. This keeps both the bottom edge and enemy entry smooth.
